label: original-phase input of 1/p/q/j/3/2/u after a prefix rich in l/a/r/w/z/o/x/e
predicate: (phase == 0) & isin(in_tok, [tok("1"), tok("p"), tok("q"), tok("j"), tok("3"), tok("2"), tok("u")]) & (n_seen([tok("l"), tok("a"), tok("r"), tok("w"), tok("z"), tok("o"), tok("x"), tok("e")]) >= 2)
explanation: Sparse (~1% of steps), 96% of mass in the original (input) phase, mostly t=2..8; it never fires at t=0, rarely at t=1, and is nearly silent at the delimiter and during copy. It fires when the current input is one of a small token set (1 is strongest: 8.7x lift and 34% of mass, then p, q, j, 3, 2, u), usually the first occurrence of that token. It is gated by prefix content: activation is much higher when earlier inputs include l, a, r, w, z, o, x or e (prev_tok a/l/z, prev2_tok l/a, first_tok r/w). Top examples look like r l l [1], w e l a [1], r l a [p]. Token identity alone gives precision ~0.09; requiring >=2 such prefix tokens raises dev precision to 0.23 with recall 0.54 and mass recall 0.67. The rest looks like a distributed dependence on hidden state that no simple predicate captures. Tokens outside the set (v, h, z, c) give weaker activations that this predicate misses.
